item.title: Fågelle Finds Melancholy Release in Glorious Gloom
item.description: Glorious gloom permeates the musical catalogue of Swedish singer-songwriter Fågelle, and her album Bränn min jord overflows with it.

item.title: The Complacent Bliss of Bruno Mars
item.description: Bruno Mars' fourth solo album, The Romantic, is as impeccably crafted as ever, but says nothing new about his place in the world of pop.

item.title: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis Create Ecstatic Post-Hardcore Jazz
item.description: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis make fearless and non-smooth fusion with the clarity and dynamism of "post-hardcore" that wasn't around in the 1970s.

item.title: Jay-Z’s 1999 Album ‘Vol. 3’ Is His Most Aggressive
item.description: In Jay-Z's Vol. 3… Life & Times of S. Carter, the ever-undeterred MC sounds anything but as he fulminates on one end and tightens his durag on the other.

item.title: ‘Slow Stories’ Combines Brian Eno’s Music with Bette A.’s Ambient Fiction
item.description: Brian Eno and Bette A. are on the same aesthetic page with Slow Stories, wherein the two form a kind of high-concept ASMR experience.

item.title: Indie Folk’s the Lowest Pair Embrace Challenges
item.description: The Lowest Pair's new record is steady and confident. It sounds like both a journey and its end point, and in finding peace within turbulent seas.

item.title: All Hail Clifton Chenier the King of Zydeco
item.description: Everybody ought to dive into the wild, eclectic, joyful zydeco of Clifton Chenier. Even the accordion averse might decide they love it.

item.title: Morrissey Is an Incorrigible Sentimentalist
item.description: Morrissey's Make-Up Is a Lie is a love letter to Paris: schmaltzy, befuddling, arresting, but, most of all, HIM.

item.title: Remembering Éliane Radigue: Godmother of Drone
item.description: People say that there are four oceans, but one could reasonably argue that there's a fifth: the one created by Éliane Radigue and her legion of cosmic drones.

item.title: Bad Bunny and the Joyful Perreo Resistance
item.description: Bad Bunny's Super Bowl LX half-time show is much more than a choreographic display; it's a manifesto of political autonomy and joyful visual sovereignty.
